text:
Sam Reinhart is doing the Sam Reinhart things. He has 12 goals and 23 points in 25 games, 11 of them on the power play, and he plays 20 minutes a night against the other team's best (Evolving-Hockey put his competition in the 97th percentile last season). The two-time Cup winner's own chances are as strong as ever: 14.22 expected goals, so if anything he's a couple of goals light.

The worry is at even strength. With Reinhart on the ice at 5v5, the Panthers have only 47.66% of the expected goals, nearly five points worse than when he sits. And his points are being helped by finishing around him: Florida has scored 7.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him out there. So the shooting looks sustainable, the on-ice results less so. Our numbers project 35 goals and 73 points. Watch whether his line starts winning its shifts again, because the power play can't carry every night.
headline: Sam Reinhart keeps scoring, but the line is leaking
